Local search, booking and AI visibility audit

Rodizio Grill Brazilian Steakhouse
Orlando

We checked everywhere a diner can find Rodizio Grill at Pointe Orlando: Google's search results and AI answers, Google Maps, Bing, Yelp, Tripadvisor, OpenTable, the delivery and catering apps, Facebook, Instagram, TikTok and YouTube, the Florida state records, and the restaurant's own website. This page shows what we found, why it matters, and the steps that fix it. Every screenshot opens full size when tapped, and every step has a box to tick when it is done.

Do these eight things this week

Every step here is free unless its cost line says otherwise. Tap a step to read how to do it. Tick the box when it is finished. This phone or computer remembers the ticks, and the Share progress button at the bottom of the page copies them as a code for another device.

  1. Step 1Done
    Replace the Pensacola phone number in the Orlando page's code and add the full address.
    The Orlando web page carries a short block of code called schema, which tells Google and the AI assistants the restaurant's name, address and phone in a form they read directly. On October 1, 2026, that code gave Orlando's phone as 850-466-2113. A Google search for that number returns only the Rodizio Grill in Pensacola. The same code gives the address as "United States" with no street, city or ZIP code. As a result, the one place where the website speaks to search engines in their own format connects Orlando to another restaurant's phone line and to no street address.
    Website vendorThe schema block on rodiziogrill.com/orlando/ and rodiziogrill.com/orlando/orlando-restaurant.aspxVendor time, which we estimate at one to two hours

    Step by step, from the official instructions
    1. On every location page, set the schema type to Restaurant and the name to the trade name every platform uses.
    2. Add servesCuisine, priceRange, a menu URL that points to an HTML menu with prices, geo coordinates within 100 meters of the entrance, openingHoursSpecification for every day and service, acceptsReservations, a potentialAction for reservations and ordering, and sameAs links to the Google listing, Yelp, Tripadvisor, the reservation platform, Facebook, Instagram and the delivery storefronts.
    3. Publish the menu as text with prices, not only as a PDF, because Google transcribes menus from the website and AI answers quote them.
    4. Put the reservation widget and the Order Online link in the main navigation and above the fold on a phone.

    Source: Google Search Central's LocalBusiness structured data page (the Restaurant example) and DoorDash's order-link placement guidance. We read it on October 1, 2026, and the platform can change its screens at any time.

  2. Step 2Done
    Correct the street number on Bing from 9191 to 9101 International Dr #1220.
    Bing, Microsoft's search engine, shows the restaurant at "9191 International Dr, Orlando, FL" with no suite number. Every other listing we opened shows 9101. Bing's listing carries a verified badge, so someone already manages it, and Bing's results also feed Microsoft's Copilot assistant and Windows maps. A diner who copies Bing's address into a map app is sent to a different building on International Drive.
    Location managerBing Places for Business$0
    How to do it, and the proof

    The location manager signs in to Bing Places with the account that verified the listing, opens the Orlando location, changes the street line to "9101 International Dr" and the second line to "#1220", and saves. Bing can also copy the details from the Google listing, which already shows the right address. If nobody knows which account verified the listing, Bing Places support can transfer it.

    Bring the Uber Eats store in line with DoorDash, or close it.
    An Uber Eats store named "Rodizio Grill Orlando" is live, and it ranks on the first page of Google for "rodizio grill orlando menu" along with a matching Postmates page. It charges $19.99 for the half-pound of grilled meats, while DoorDash and the restaurant's own ordering page charge $17.00. It shows the lowest price tier, a single "$", lists menu hours of 5:00 to 9:00 PM against 5:00 to 8:40 PM on DoorDash, and spells a menu section "Al Acarte". Bing uses its rating of 5 from 5 reviews as one of the restaurant's three scores. A diner who sees two different prices for the same dish trusts neither.

  4. Step 4Done
    Mark the restaurant's own ordering page as preferred on Google, and switch Takeout and Delivery on.
    The Order online button on Google offers two choices: "Online Ordering by DoorDash," which is the restaurant's own branded ordering page that DoorDash runs for it, and the DoorDash marketplace app. Neither carries Google's "Preferred by this business" label. DoorDash's help center states that orders placed through the marketplace from Google give the restaurant no customer email or phone. At the same time, Google Maps lists the restaurant's service options as Dine-in yes, Takeout no and Delivery no, so a diner sees an Order button next to a line saying the restaurant does not offer takeout.
    Location managerGoogle Business Profile, Food ordering and Edit profile$0
    How to do it, and the proof

    The delivery fees in the dialog favor the marketplace for the diner, so the owner chooses which of the two DoorDash options to mark preferred after weighing the customer data against the fee the diner sees.

    LinksManage the Google listingGoogle's instructions for online ordering providersDoorDash on Order with Google and the preferred providerGoogle's help community for problems
    Step by step, from the official instructions
    1. Go to the Business Profile and select Food ordering.
    2. Turn Accept orders on your profile on or off. Off hides every third-party option.
    3. Select the restaurant's own storefront link, select Set as preferred, turn on Preferred for pickup and for delivery, and Save. Customers then see "Preferred by this business".
    4. To remove a provider, select it and select Remove link. Google requires the provider to remove its link within 5 business days; if it does not, report a violation.
    5. DoorDash enables its Google ordering automatically for restaurants that have Online Ordering in their plan, so check the dialog even if nobody set it up.

    Source: Google's page "Manage online ordering options" and DoorDash's "Order With Google" overview. We read it on October 1, 2026, and the platform can change its screens at any time.

    LinksManage the Google listingGoogle's attribute instructionsWhy an edit shows as pending or not approved
    Step by step, from the official instructions
    1. Go to the Business Profile, select Edit profile, then More.
    2. Next to the attribute group (Amenities, Dining options, Payments, Accessibility), select Edit, set each attribute to Yes or No, and Save.
    3. Some attributes come from customer answers and only appear as options after Google collects them; review them after the edit publishes. Review takes about 10 minutes and can take up to 30 days.

    Source: Google's page "Manage your business attributes". We read it on October 1, 2026, and the platform can change its screens at any time.

Where a diner finds the restaurant, and where the trail breaks

A diner reaches a table in six moves. The cards below name each move and what we found there.

What we found, in one look

Diners rate Rodizio Grill Orlando highly everywhere, the Google listing is well kept, and Google's AI books it first for a table near the convention center. The problems sit in the facts other systems publish about it: a wrong phone in the website's code, a wrong street number on Bing, a second price on Uber Eats, and website buttons that lead to chain pages instead of Orlando pages. Separately, the restaurant is missing from Google's map box on the main Brazilian-steakhouse searches, where a competitor pays to appear.

What does the Google listing contain today?

Needs attention

The Google Business Profile is the listing Google shows on Maps and beside search results. For a restaurant it carries a menu, a reservation button, ordering providers, dining attributes, hours, a price band that diners report, and a review summary written by Gemini, Google's AI. Orlando's listing is among the better-kept ones we have seen: the owner entered the menu a week before our check, and the newest post went up two days before it.

What we checked

We opened the listing on Google Maps and in Google Search on October 1, 2026, signed in, with Google set to Orlando. We opened the Reserve a table and Order online dialogs, the full menu, the review summary, the newest and lowest-rated reviews, and the posts. Google Maps would not open its About tab in our session, so the full list of dining and dietary attributes is still to check; the search panel shows "All you can eat, Outdoor seating, Private dining room" and "LGBTQ+ friendly".

The popular-dish names "Grilled Meats 1 2 lb" and "Salad Bar Only -" come from takeout items, not from the dining menu. The location manager can rename them in the Google Maps app, as the menu instructions below explain.

LinksManage the Google listingGoogle's menu editor instructionsGoogle's popular-dish instructionsGoogle's help community for problems
Step by step, from the official instructions
  1. Go to the Business Profile and select Edit menu above the search results.
  2. Add sections (for example Grill, Salads, Sides, Desserts, Drinks), then items with descriptions and prices, and select Save. Google displays changes within 24 to 48 hours.
  3. Where Google offers to copy an existing menu from a third-party source, check the source first, because that source may carry old prices.
  4. To correct a dish name a customer added, open the Google Maps app, open the Menu tab, tap the dish, and use Suggest an edit to rename it, mark it incorrect, or mark it not served here.
  5. A chain that updates menus across many profiles must use the Business Profile API.

Source: Google's pages "About the menu editor" and "Manage your restaurant's popular dish names". We read it on October 1, 2026, and the platform can change its screens at any time.

How does a diner book a table or place an order, and what stands in the way?

Needs attention

OpenTable handles Orlando's reservations on the website, on Google and in Google's AI Mode, and the whole path works. DoorDash handles ordering through two channels: a branded ordering page in the restaurant's name and the DoorDash app. Uber Eats keeps a third store with different prices. Bookings from Google come through Reserve with Google, the program that lets Google show a partner's live tables.

Step by step, from the official instructions
  1. Confirm the restaurant is live and accepting reservations on its platform (OpenTable, Yelp Guest Manager, Resy, Tock or another Reserve with Google partner).
  2. Confirm that the name, address and phone on the platform closely match the Google listing; OpenTable states that a mismatch stops availability from showing on Google.
  3. If availability still does not appear, contact the platform's account team to confirm the partner feed is turned on.
  4. For a waitlist button, go to the Business Profile, select Waitlists, select Get started, and follow the setup with an eligible provider. Removing the button requires unregistering with the provider.

What do diners read in the reviews?

Working

Every platform rates Orlando between 4.2 and 4.9. Google reviews arrive at about ten a day, and the restaurant answers each one within a few hours by name. Yelp is the weak spot: reviews arrive about twice a month, and only about half of the newest ten carry a reply.

What diners praise, by Google's topic counts
  • The salad bar, in 311 reviews.
  • Kind staff, in 215 reviews, often by a server's first name.
  • The gauchos who carve at the table, in 119 reviews.
  • The grilled pineapple, in 48 reviews, and the flan, the dish Yelp diners mention most.
What diners complain about in the reviews we read
  • Tough or gamey beef cuts, in the newest one-star Google review, two months old.
  • Long gaps between meat passes, in a five-month-old one-star review.
  • A table request ignored for a guest with visual and mobility needs, on OpenTable five days before our check.
  • Value for the price, which Bing's AI summary and OpenTable's lowest sub-score both raise.
Why this mattersBrightLocal's 2026 survey of consumers, which is a vendor's own research, found that 68% require a 4.0 rating, 31% now use only businesses rated 4.5 or higher, and 74% care only about reviews from the last three months. Orlando clears 4.0 everywhere. Yelp at 4.4 and OpenTable at 4.2 sit just under the 4.5 line, and Yelp's ten newest reviews stretch back five and a half months.

What we checked

We read Google's newest reviews from the three days before October 1, 2026, Google's lowest-rated reviews, Yelp's ten newest reviews, OpenTable's review summary and newest review, and the scores on Tripadvisor, Facebook and DoorDash. LinksManage the Google listingGoogle's instructions for replying to reviewsThe FTC rule on fake and paid reviews
Step by step, from the official instructions
  1. Go to the Business Profile and select Read reviews.
  2. Next to the review, select Reply, write the reply, and select Reply again. Google checks it, usually within 10 minutes and sometimes up to 30 days, then posts it under the review.
  3. When asking guests for reviews, offer no reward that depends on a positive review, and have staff and family disclose any connection; the FTC rule of August 2024 prohibits both practices with civil penalties.

Source: Google's page "Manage customer reviews" and the FTC's final rule announcement (August 14, 2024). We read it on October 1, 2026, and the platform can change its screens at any time.

What did we find on the restaurant's own website?

Broken right now

The Orlando page states every fact a diner needs in plain text: prices, children's prices, hours by service, parking, both phone numbers and the event contact. The problems sit in the parts diners do not see: the code Google reads, the sitemap, the links to other pages, and the page's speed on a phone.

What works
  • The page lists every price, including children's prices and the salad-only option, as text Google can read.
  • The reservations page uses OpenTable's own widget, and a Book a Table bar stays on screen on a phone.
  • The site lets every search engine and AI crawler read it, and the server answers in 60 milliseconds.
  • The chain menu page links a current allergy list dated May 2026.
What is broken or missing
  • The page's code. It gives Pensacola's phone, no street address, and none of the hours, prices, menu or booking links Google's restaurant example includes.
  • Speed on a phone. Google's Lighthouse test scored the page 48 of 100. The main image took 11.3 seconds to appear, and the layout shifted by 0.254, both in Google's "poor" range.
  • Two Orlando pages. A second page, /orlando/orlando-restaurant.aspx, competes with the main page in Google's results.
  • The sitemap. The sitemap, the file that lists a site's pages for Google, holds ten chain pages and no location page.
  • Phone layout. The heading "ORLANDO, FLORIDA" runs off the right edge, and the bar's Order button is cut off.
  • Questions the page does not answer. Dress code, group sizes and private rooms, dietary options, and holiday hours.
Show the details and the proof

We read the Orlando page, the reservations page, the second Orlando page, the chain menu page, robots.txt (the file that tells crawlers what they may read), the sitemap and llms.txt on October 1, 2026. The menu page shows no prices in its text, so Orlando's prices live only on the Orlando page and in Google's menu. The site has no llms.txt file; published research has found no measurable effect from that file, so we do not list it as a step. The speed test is a lab test on a simulated mid-range phone over a slow mobile connection, not a measure of real visitors.

AI Mode: find a table for 4 at a Brazilian steakhouse near the Orange County Convention Center Saturday at 7 pm
AI Mode listed Rodizio Grill Orlando first, under "Closest to the Convention Center," with a Reserve a table button and a 6:45 PM table. It then listed Fogo de Chão without a booking button, and Divina Carne and BoiBrazil with one. It offered to book Rodizio.

What do the Florida state records show?

Working

Florida's Division of Hotels and Restaurants inspects the restaurant under food license SEA5811756. Florida Today's public copy of the state's inspection data shows that both 2026 inspections, on January 13 and August 11, ended "Met Inspection Standards," with five and four violations noted. It names Rodizio OpCo LLC as the licensee, while the "Rodizio Grill Orlando" trade name belongs to Fenix I-Drive, LLC. The owner confirms which company operates the restaurant, because the state, the ad platforms and the delivery apps should all name the same one.

How we checked, what we could not see, and how this page works

How we checked. We opened every page named here on October 1, 2026 in Chrome, signed in to a Google account, with "Orlando" or an Orlando landmark typed into every search. We read the Florida Division of Corporations records, the Orlando web pages and their code, the Google listing and its dialogs, OpenTable, Yelp, Tripadvisor, Bing, Apple Maps, MapQuest, YellowPages, the BBB, Pointe Orlando's directory, DoorDash, the branded ordering page, Uber Eats, ezCater, Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, Reddit, Google's Ads Transparency Center and Meta's Ad Library.

Where the screenshots come from. Every small picture on this page is a capture of the public page named in its caption, taken on October 1, 2026. The schema picture is the page's code copied as text, as its caption says.

What we could not see. We could not see the owner's dashboards on Google, OpenTable, DoorDash or Uber Eats, the OpenTable plan, or Google's count of searches and bookings. Google Maps would not open the listing's About tab or the Ask Maps question in our session, and Apple Maps did not load its full card, so those join the first monthly re-run. We did not test ChatGPT, Gemini or Copilot, did not search TikTok while signed in, and did not open the data companies' paid records. The state's license search did not return the inspection record, so the inspection dates come from Florida Today's copy of the state data. The speed figures come from a lab test, not from real visitors.

Where the links come from. Every listing task carries links to the page where the listing is managed, to the platform's own instructions, and to a support or problems page, plus a step-by-step drop-down that repeats the platform's instructions in plain words with the date we read them.

How the check boxes work. The ticks are saved on the phone or computer where they were made. The Share progress button copies a progress code. Pasting that code into the box at the bottom of the page on another device adds the same ticks there. The Concise and Detailed buttons open or close every detail block at once.
